description:
Found by the fz-kdt.127 research (2026-09-02, HEAD 172ab21f1, r3/report.md Q4).
callable_flow_resolution_edges_product (jobs/runtime_demand.rs:3166) mints
activation_key(root, lambda, capture_tys ++ surface.inputs) (:3218) per
first-class SURFACE demanded at a callable position. At an erased forwarder
(fz-6gb: `run` keyed `(a0_p0) -> a0_r`) the demand of ALL callers is joined
(arg_demands_for_summary :2746) and flows back to EVERY mint site
(record_first_class_boundary_demand :3064/:3093), so each mint is credited
with every other mint's arg surfaces: the correlation between a capture and
the args it is actually called with is lost at the forwarder join.

Measured: samelambda3 (scratchpad sl3.fz) mints P.mk/1#lambda at 4
(capture x arg) keys, 3 reachable, `[int capture, float arg]` DEAD --
analyzed, lowered, shipped as wrapper member x11. 00277
`Enum.reverse/1#lambda[int, list(int | :tail)]` dead (that accumulator
arises only from reverse/2's own lambda and reaches reverse/1's lambda
through the shared erased Range.reduce_cont/6 slot 5). Corpus: 110 of 354
construction wrappers have >= 2 members.

This is excess work (proportional compilation), not a correctness break:
the wrapper's runtime selection never routes a value to a dead member.
Characterize the reachable set per mint (capture x the args that mint's
value actually flows to), measure the dead fraction corpus-wide, and
decide whether the product should be correlated per mint site or pruned
by reachability. Independent of fz-kdt.127's read-side fix (which does
not change this product -- verify after it lands).
title: The callable-flow product mints dead (capture x arg) activations from demand joined at an erased forwarder
